topic: Paediatric buckle and forearm fracture management
usual_baseline: Buckle fractures are over-treated: rigid casts in 22–100% [1271, 1765], 95.4% full cast in clinic [1692], fracture clinic follow-up in 43–58% [1307, 1765], and discharge at first visit in 7.7% [1692]. For displaced forearm fractures, national BOAST compliance is 63%, with post-manipulation neurovascular checks in 35% and consent in 38% [1758].
fix_that_works: Guideline revision, leaflets and education cut plaster casts from 34% to 10% and clinic follow-up from 43% to 17% [1307]. Parent education and email reminders gave 62/64 direct ED discharges [1651]. Teaching raised NICE compliance from 56% to 80% at a DGH [1765]. A BOAST pathway raised ED manipulation from 23/72 to 73/87 [1648]. An ED SOP cut theatre need from 36.4% to 1.9% [1663].
fix_that_fails: The same teaching reached only 31% compliance at an MIU, where rigid immobilisation stayed at 69% [1765]. After a new pathway, first-visit discharge was still only 44.8% and 47.1% kept a cast [1692]. Neurovascular documentation before discharge stayed at 64.36% and clinic within 7 days at 49.42% [1648].
consultant_advice: Buckle fracture audits are common and the fix is well known. Check splint stock and cover minor injury units, where rigid casts persist. More useful is the forearm manipulation pathway: ED versus theatre reduction, failed reductions, consent and post-manipulation neurovascular checks, which national data show are weak [1758].
